 42 bar / 480 °C (896°F).

offers.detailsText:
American Plant & Equipment is actively sourcing the equipment described below. If you can supply it, please reply with your best quotation: unit price, key specifications, condition, availability, photos and delivery terms. Reference N-8886 in your response.
 We are looking to purchase the following:
 OUR REF: N-8886
 Gas-fired Jenbacher, 1 MW power generation package / gas engine generator set
 1. Quotation requested for a gas-fired power generation package providing 1000 kW site electrical demand. The application uses low-BTU, high-inert special gas rather than standard pipeline natural gas, so a suitable special-gas/biogas engine version with wide Wobbe-index tolerance is required. Surplus or used equipment is preferred, subject to availability and condition; new or factory-reconditioned equipment is also acceptable if faster to deliver. Include gas conditioning equipment for pressure letdown, filtration/coalescing, temperature control, and dewpoint conditioning from the 985 psia battery-limit supply to the engine inlet requirements.
 2. 1000 kW site electrical demand
 3. 400 V, 50 Hz
 4. fuel gas GHV approximately 341 Btu/scf
 5. battery-limit pressure 985 psia
 6. gas temperature 45°F
 7. composition: N₂ 40.9 mol%, CO₂ 27.3 mol%, CH₄ 30.0 mol%, C2+ approximately 1.8 mol%, H₂S nil
 8. total inerts approximately 68.2 mol%
 9. special-gas/biogas engine with wide Wobbe-index tolerance, such as Jenbacher GS-B.L/GS-S.L class or equivalent
 10. site elevation 295–328 ft
 11. ambient dry-bulb 32–125°F (0–52°C)
 12. maximum wet-bulb 89°F (31.7°C)
 13. relative humidity 35–60%
 14. seismic zone 2B
 15. wind speed 100 mph
 16. derate based on 52°C maximum dry-bulb temperature
 17. altitude is not limiting
 18. no gas compression required
 19. fuel gas conditioning and gas train scope required.
 20. Notes: Please confirm suitable model(s), rated output at site conditions and derating basis at 52°C, expected fuel gas flow at the stated composition, minimum gas-train pressure at the engine skid inlet, methane number/inert tolerance, delivery time, commercial offer, and availability status. Used or surplus equipment is preferred, subject to condition. Gas is available at 985 psia at the battery limit and must be let down and conditioned; no compression is needed.
 If you have any, please email us. We need full details, price, and photos.

 Gearbox output shaft is connected to the electric generator.
 Main lube oil pump mounted on the gearbox gear NDE shaft, providing availability of lubricating oil for lubrication and cooling for a significant time even under blackout conditions.

 Lubricating Oil System Steam turbine and gearbox assembly mounted on a single base frame with under-base lubrication oil tank.
 All lube oil and control oil pipes, lube oil pumps and other components are mounted within the skid and are factory assembled.

 Integrated lube oil tank and piping, reducing site piping and installation work.
 Compact skid design, resulting in reduced equipment footprint.
 Reduced erection and commissioning time due to maximum factory pre-assembly.
 Reduced site manpower and installation complexity, ensuring faster and more reliable project execution.

 CACW cooling arrangement.
 AVR comprising auto and manual (1A+1M) mode (ABB make model 1010) used for voltage / PF controlling.

 Neutral side cubicle also houses current transformers for input to relays and metering system.
 AC motors, S1 duty rating and grade IE2, TEFC, IP55 with DOL starting method.
 DC motor, 110 V DC, TEFC, IP 54 protection.
 Wall mounted DC starter panel with 2 step resistors start system.
 MCC cubicle serves as the auxiliary motor control centre, managing power distribution and control for all auxiliary motors and associated equipment.

 STG Control & Supervisory System STG supervisory panel provides turbine governing, supervisory monitoring and critical protection functions for safe and reliable operation of the steam turbine generator.

 Panel incorporates a dedicated overspeed protection system for independent protection against turbine overspeed.
 Panel provides necessary indications, alarms, permissive and trip interfaces associated with the turbine.
 Panel has suitable communication and hardwired interface provisions with the customer's central control system (PLC/DCS) for coordinated start-up, operation, monitoring, alarm and trip functions.

 Sequence descriptions, cause and effect, interlock/permissive logic and relevant I/O/interface details are provided for implementation in the customer's PLC/DCS.

 FUELS & EMISSIONS
 PRIMARY FUEL: NATURAL GAS — EXCELLENT PERFORMANCE AND LOW EMISSIONS.
 FUEL FLEXIBLE: LNG, LOW-CALORIFIC / SOUR GASES (CONTAINING CO₂, H₂S, N₂), DISTILLATE OIL, CRUDE / HEAVY FUEL OIL, BIODIESEL, KEROSENE, CONDENSATE, AND OTHERS ON REQUEST. DUAL-FUEL CAPABLE.
 NOX CONTROLLED EFFECTIVELY ON NATURAL GAS VIA DRY LOW-NOX (DLE) OR HYBRID BURNERS.

 FULL COMBINED-CYCLE PLANT: GT + HRSG + STEAM TURBINE + BALANCE OF PLANT — SUBSTANTIALLY LARGER AND SITE-SPECIFIC

 KEY FEATURES & BENEFITS
 HIGH RELIABILITY AND AVAILABILITY FOR CONTINUOUS OR CYCLIC OPERATION.
 FAST START-UP AND GOOD TRANSIENT RESPONSE; VARIABLE INLET GUIDE VANES SUPPORT GRID FREQUENCY.
 EASY MAINTENANCE: ACCESSIBLE SILO COMBUSTORS; INDIVIDUALLY REPLACEABLE BLADES / VANES (OFTEN WITHOUT FULL ROTOR LIFT); ON-SITE ROTOR DE-STACKING POSSIBLE.
 STRONG CYCLING CAPABILITY AND HYDRAULIC CLEARANCE OPTIMIZATION FOR PROTECTION DURING TRANSIENTS.
 PROVEN IN NUMEROUS REFERENCE PLANTS WORLDWIDE.

 EMISSIONS & ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE

BOTH UNITS HAVE UNDERGONE A COMPLETE SIEMENS ‑ SUPERVISED REBUILD PROCESS, RESTORING THEM TO “AS ‑ NEW” CONDITION IN ACCORDANCE WITH OEM STANDARDS. THIS INCLUDES FULL DISASSEMBLY, COMPONENT ‑ LEVEL REFURBISHMENT, REPLACEMENT OF LIFE ‑ LIMITED PARTS, AND REASSEMBLY UNDER SIEMENS QUALITY PROTOCOLS.  B. Description
 1. The source describes the Siemens SGT-A05 model as a compact, lightweight industrial aeroderivative gas turbine designed for decentralized power generation, standby power, cogeneration, combined heat and power, mobile power, emergency power, and oil and gas applications.
 2. The source describes the model as offering high efficiency, strong performance, and fast-start capability, reaching full power in approximately 60 seconds.

 C. Model-Level Specifications and Options
 1. Electrical power output: up to 5.8 MW(e); exact unit output is not stated
 2. Frequency/voltage: the model is available for 50 Hz and 60 Hz applications, with various configurations and voltage outputs available; exact unit configuration is not stated
 3. Supported fuel options: natural gas, liquid fuel, dual fuel, and mid-to-low BTU gas; exact unit configuration is not stated
 4. Available emissions options: Wet Low Emissions and Dry Low Emissions systems; exact unit configuration is not stated
 5. Model capability: full engine power within 60 seconds; black-start capability
 6. Package design: single-trailer, self-contained mobile package
 7. Source states that on-site setup and on-site commissioning each take less than 2 hours
 8. Source-stated rapid response: full power within 1 minute of starting
 9. Available low-noise option: less than 85 dBA near-field and less than 65 dBC far-field
 10. Model-level claim: up to 32,000 baseload-duty hours between full overhauls; unit overhaul status is not stated
 11. Model-level claim: over 98% demonstrated availability/reliability; this is not a unit-specific operating record
 12. Source states that SGT-A05 variants are built to meet quality standards including ISO 9001 and AS9100
 13. Model designed for in-field servicing, including direct core-engine exchange in a single 8-hour work shift

 D. Package Features (installed scope to be confirmed)
 1. Switchgear enclosure: switchgear, unit control panel, motor control center, starter control panel, auxiliary transformer, purge air cooler, and instrument air compressor
 2. Five-axle trailer: steerable forward two axles, lifting forward axle, cross-wind-rated design, and ten landing legs
 3. Ventilated enclosure: gas turbine, synthetic GT lube oil system, air inlet silencers, GT enclosure ventilation, fire protection system, dual gas fuel inlets, ventilation air inlets, gearbox, and A/C generator
 4. Exhaust enclosure: exhaust enclosure cover, enclosure ventilation exhaust, and lubrication oil cooler
 5. Additional source-described systems: on-skid fuel system; air-intake filter assembly, silencer, and flow-direction geometry; acoustic gas turbine enclosure; and water-wash system. Extreme-environment filtration is described as available.

 E. Model Applications Identified in Source
 1. Prime power for remote operations, including oil and gas and mining
 2. Temporary power demand for military, government, construction, utilities, and drilling
 3. Peaking and transmission congestion relief
 4. Standby emergency power; temporary-outage replacement for aged power plants in developed countries
 5. Critical process power for chemical, pharmaceutical, data hub, hospital, and university applications
 6. Distributed generation for grid support
